﴿ولو شاء لجعله ساكنا﴾ مستقرا على تلك الحالة، ثم خلق الشمس وجعله على ذلك الظل سلطها عليه وجعلها دليلا متبوعا لهم كما يتبع الدليل في الطريق، فهو يزيد بها وينقص ويمتد ويقلص، ثم نسخه بها قبضه قبضا سهلا يسيرا غير عسير. ويحتمل أن يريد قبضه عند قيام الساعة بقبض أسبابه، وهي الأجرام التي تلقي الظل، فيكون قد ذكر إعدامه بإعدام أسبابه، كما ذكر إنشاءه بإنشاء أسبابه، وقوله: (قبضناه إلينا) يدل عليه، وكذلك قوله: (يسيرا)، كما قال: ﴿ذلك حشر علينا يسير﴾ [Qaf: 44] [*"That is a gathering easy for Us."*]، انتهى. وقوله: سمى انبساط الظل وامتداده تحركا منه، لم يسم الله ذلك، إنما قال: (كيف مد الظل). وقوله: ويحتمل أن يريد قبضه عند قيام الساعة، فهذا يبعد احتماله؛ لأنه إنما ذكر آثار صنعته وقدرته لتشاهد، ثم قال: (مد الظل) وعطف عليه ماضيا مثله، فيبعد أن يكون التقدير: ثم قبضه عند قيام الساعة، مع ظهور كونه ماضيا مستدامًا أمثاله.

وقال ابن عطية: ﴿ولو شاء لجعله ساكنا﴾، أي: ثابتا غير متحرك ولا منسوخ، لكنه جعل الشمس ونسخها إياه (p-٥٠٤) بطردها له من موضع إلى موضع دليلا عليه، مبينا لوجوده ولوجه العبرة فيه. وحكى الطبري: أنه لولا الشمس لم يعلم أن الظل شيء، إذ الأشياء إنما تعرف بأضدادها. وقال ابن عباس: (يسيرا) معجلا. وقال مجاهد: لطيفا، أي: شيئا بعد شيء، ويحتمل أن يريد سهلا قريب التناول. وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: أكثر الناس في تأويل هذه الآية، ويُرفع الكلام فيها إلى وجهين.

الأول: أن الظل لا ضوء خالص ولا ظلمة خالصة، وهو ما بين طلوع الفجر وطلوع الشمس، وكذلك الكيفيات الحاصلة داخل السقف وأبنية الجدارات، وهي أطيب الأحوال؛ لأن الظلمة الخالصة يكرهها الطبع وينفر عنها الحس، والضوء الخالص يحير الحس البصري ويحدث السخونة القوية، وهي مؤذية، ولهذا قيل في الجنة: ﴿وظل ممدود﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 30] [*"and extended shade"*]، والناظر إلى الجسم الملون كأنه يشاهد بالظل شيئا سوى الجسم وسوى اللون، والظل ليس أمرا ثالثا ولا معرفة به إلا أنه إذا طلعت الشمس ووقع ضوؤها على الجسم ثم مال، عرف للظل وجود وماهية، ولولاها ما عرف؛ لأن الأشياء تدرك بأضدادها، فظهر للعقل أن الظل كيفية زائدة على الجسم واللون؛ ولذلك قال: ﴿ثم جعلنا الشمس عليه دليلا﴾، أي: جعلنا الظل أولا بما فيه من المنافع واللذات، ثم هدينا العقول إلى معرفة وجوده بأن أطلعنا الشمس فكانت دليلا على وجود الظل. (ثم قبضناه) أي: أزلناه لا دفعة بل (يسيرا) يسيرا، كلما ازداد ارتفاع الشمس ازداد نقصان الظل من جانب المغرب، ولما كانت الحركات المكانية لا توجد دفعة بل يسيرا يسيرا كان زوال الأظلال كذلك.

والثاني: أنه لما خلق السماء والأرض وقع ظل السماء على الأرض، فجعل الشمس دليلا؛ لأنه بحسب حركات الأضواء تتحرك الأظلال، فهما متعاقبان متلازمان لا واسطة بينهما، فبمقدار ما يزداد أحدهما ينقص الآخر، فكما أن المهتدي يقتدي بالهادي والدليل ويلازمه فكذلك الأظلال ملازمة للأضواء، ولذلك جعل الشمس دليلا عليه، انتهى ملخصا. وهو مأخوذ من كلام الزمخشري، ومحسن بعض تحسين. والآية في غاية الظهور ولا تحتاج إلى هذا التكثير.

وقال أيضا: الظل ليس عدما محضا، بل هو أضواء مخلوطة بظلام، فهو أمر وجودي، وفي تحقيقه دقيق يرجع فيه إلى الكتب العقلية، انتهى. والآية في غاية الوضوح ولا تحتاج إلى هذا التكثير، وقد تركت أشياء من كلام المفسرين مما لا تمس إليه الحاجة. (جعل الليل لباسا) تشبيها بالثوب الذي يغطي البدن ويستره؛ من حيث الليل يستر الأشياء. والسبات: ضرب من الإغماء يعتري اليقظان مرضا، فشبه النوم به، والسبت الإقامة في المكان، فكان السبات سكونا تاما، والنشور هنا الإحياء، شبه اليقظة به ليتطابق الإحياء مع الإماتة، اللذين يتضمنهما النوم والسبات، انتهى من كلام ابن عطية. وقال غيره: السبات الراحة، جعل النوم سباتا أي: سبب راحة.

وقال الزمخشري: السبات الموت، وهو كقوله: ﴿وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل﴾ [al-An'am: 60] [*"It is He who takes you in death by night."*]. (فإن قلت): هلا فسرته بالراحة؟ (قلت): النشور في مقابلته يأباه، انتهى. ولا يأباه إلا لو تعين تفسير النشور بالحياة. وقال أبو مسلم: (نشورا) هو بمعنى الانتشار والحركة. وقال ابن عطية: ويحتمل أن يريد بالنشور وقت انتشار وتفرق لطلب المعاش وابتغاء فضل الله. و(النهار نشورا) وما قبله من باب: ليل نائم ونهار صائم، وهذه الآية مع دلالتها على قدرة الخالق، فيها إظهار لنعمته على خلقه؛ لأن الاحتجاب بستر الليل كم فيه لكثير من الناس فوائد دينية ودنيوية. وقال الشاعر:

*وكم لظلام الليل عندي من يد* 
*تخبر أن المانوية تكذب*

[*"How many a favour of the darkness of night is mine, which proves that the Manichaeans lie."*]

والنوم واليقظة وشبههما بالموت والحياة، أي: عبرة فيهما لمن اعتبر. وعن لقمان أنه قال لابنه: يا بني كما (p-٥٠٥) تنام فتوقظ فكذلك تموت فتنشر.

The disagreement over the recitation of **al-rīḥ** (the wind) as singular or plural was discussed earlier, in al-Baqarah. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: The plural recitation is more apt, because the usage of *al-rīḥ* in the Qur'an, whenever it appears in the singular, refers to punishment, while whenever it refers to rain and mercy it appears as *riyāḥ* (winds). This is because the wind of rain spreads out, shifts, scatters, and comes gently, from here and there and one thing after another, whereas the wind of punishment comes out without shifting, arriving as one solid body. Do you not see that it smashes and demolishes whatever it finds? Al-Rummānī said: The winds of mercy are plural because there are three fertilizing (*lawāqiḥ*) winds: the south wind, the east wind, and the north wind. The wind of punishment is singular because it is one wind that does not fertilize, namely the west wind (*al-dabūr*). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: The saying of the Prophet ﷺ refutes this, when a wind blew: "O Allah, make it winds (*riyāḥan*) and do not make it a single wind (*rīḥan*)." End of quote. It is not appropriate to say that this recitation is more apt, because each of the two recitations is *mutawātir* (transmitted by a large number of narrators through every stage, so that its authenticity is certain), and the *alif* and *lām* in *al-rīḥ* are for the category, so they are generalizing. As for what was mentioned, that al-Rummānī's statement is refuted by the hadith, this is not evident, because it is possible that by his words ﷺ "*riyāḥan*" he meant the three fertilizing winds, and by "do not make it a single wind" he meant the west wind. Thus what al-Rummānī said agrees with the hadith on this understanding.

The disagreement over the recitation of **nushran** (spreading out) and its meaning was discussed in al-Aʿrāf. The phrase ﴿before His mercy﴾ is a fine metaphor, meaning in front of the rain, because it comes heralded by it. *Ṭahūr* is on the pattern *faʿūl*, either for emphasis, like *naʾūm* (very sleepy), in which case it is derived from *ṭāhir* (pure); or it is a noun for what is used for purification, like *saḥūr* (pre-dawn meal) and *faṭūr* (breakfast); or it is a verbal noun of *tatahhara* (to purify oneself), coming in a form other than the regular verbal noun, as transmitted by Sībawayh. The apparent sense of His words ﴿pure water﴾ is that it is for emphasis on its purity. The basis of the emphasis is that nothing has mixed with it, unlike water that springs from the earth and the like, which is mixed with earthy particles from its place of rest, its course, or what is thrown into it. It may be described as a noun or as a verbal noun. Thaʿlab said: It is what is pure in itself and purifies others. If what he said is an explanation of its intensified purity, it is sound, and it is supported by His words ﴿and He sends down upon you water from the sky to purify you by it﴾ [al-Anfāl: 11]. Otherwise, *faʿūl* does not mean *mufaʿʿil* (causative form). An example of the use of *ṭahūr* for emphasis is His words, exalted is He: ﴿And their Lord will give them a pure drink﴾ [al-Insān: 21]. The poet said:

*To smooth-hipped gazelles of the deer, with sweet teeth, whose saliva is pure*

The recitation of ʿĪsā and Abū Jaʿfar was "*mayyitan*" (with a shadda), and they described *baldatan* (town) with a masculine adjective, because *al-baldah* has the meaning of *al-balad* in His words ﴿so We drove it to a dead land﴾ [Fāṭir: 9]. The majority preferred the lightened form, because it resembles a verbal noun of the form *faʿl*; just as the masculine and feminine are described by a verbal noun, so too by what resembles it, unlike the doubled form, which resembles the active participle *fāʿil* in accepting the feminine *tāʾ*, except in what is specific to the feminine, such as *ṭāmith* (menstruating).

ʿAbd Allāh, Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim, and Abū ʿAmr, in one narration from them, recited "*wa-nasqiyahu*" (and We give it to drink) with a fatḥa on the nūn. It is also narrated from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. Yaḥyā ibn al-Ḥārith al-Dhimārī recited "*wa-anāsiya*" with the yāʾ lightened. It is narrated from al-Kisāʾī: "*wa-anāsiyya*," the plural of *insān* in the view of Sībawayh, and the plural of *insī* in the view of al-Farrāʾ, al-Mubarrad, and al-Zajjāj. The regular plural would be *anāsiyya*, as they said for *muhallabī* the plural *mahālibah*. It is also reported that the plural of *insān* is *anāsīn*, like *sirḥān* and *sarāḥīn*.

He described the water as pure and gave as the reason for sending it down the giving of life and drink, because since the humans are among those for whom the water was sent down, it was described as pure, both as an honor to them and as completing the blessing upon them. The causal clause implies that purity is a condition for the validity of this, just as you would say: "The prince mounted me on a swift horse so that I might hunt wild game on it."

He placed the reviving of the land and the watering of livestock before the watering of humans, because their life depends on the life of their land and the life of their livestock. So He mentioned first what is the cause of that. Also, when they find what waters their land and their livestock, they find their own drink.

*Al-anʿām* (livestock) and *al-anāsī* were made indefinite and described as numerous, because many of them are sustained only by the rain that Allah sends down. Likewise, ﴿that We may revive by it a dead town﴾ refers to some of the lands of these people who are far from the places where water is found, unlike the inhabitants of cities, who are near to valleys, rivers, and springs, and so are generally independent of rainwater for irrigation. He singled out livestock from among the drinking animals He created, because birds and wild beasts go far in search of water, so drinking does not fail them, unlike livestock, which are the property of humans, and their benefits depend on them. So bestowing favor upon them by watering their livestock is like bestowing favor upon them by watering them.

The pronoun in "*ṣarrafnāhu*" (We have diversified it) refers to the water sent down from the sky. That is, We made the sending down of water a reminder, by turning it from some places to others. It occurs each year in the same amount; this was said by the majority, including Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Mujāhid. According to this interpretation, "*illā kufūran*" (except disbelief) is their saying that rain comes by the stars and constellations (*anwāʾ*); this was said by ʿIkrima. It was also said that "*kufūran*" is unrestricted disbelief, since they abandoned reflection.

Ibn ʿAbbās also said: It refers to the Qur'an, even though it has not been mentioned before, because the matter is clear. This is supported by His words "*wa-jāhidhum bihi*" (and strive against them with it), for the pronouns are consistent. And if it refers to the rain, then "*bihi*" refers to the Qur'an.

Abū Muslim said: It refers to the rain, the winds, the clouds, and all the other signs mentioned in it.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: We have diversified this statement among people in the Qur'an and in all the other books and scriptures sent down to the messengers, namely the mention of the creation of clouds and the sending down of rain, so that they might reflect, take heed, recognize the right of the blessing in it, and give thanks. But most of them refused except to deny the blessing, reject it, and care little for it.

It was also said: We diversified the rain among them in different lands and different times, and in varying forms: heavy downpour, drizzle, light rain, mist, steady rain, and fine rain. But they refused except disbelief, and that they should say, "We were given rain by such-and-such a star," and not mention His mercy and His craftsmanship.

It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: No year has less rain than another, but Allah distributes it among His servants as He wills, and he recited this verse.

It is narrated that the angels know the number and quantity of the rain each year, because it does not vary, but it varies among the lands.

From this a response can be drawn regarding the indefiniteness of *al-baldah*, *al-anʿām*, and *al-anāsī*, as if He said: "That He may revive by it some dead lands, and that We may give to drink some of the livestock and humans, and that portion is many." End of quote.

ʿIkrima recited "*ṣarafnāhu*" with the rāʾ lightened.

[p. 506]

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 25, verses 51–60 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And had We willed, We would have sent a warner to every town.﴾ When the Exalted knew what the Messenger endured of harm from his people, He informed him that, had He willed, He would have sent a warner to every town, so that the matter would be lighter for you. But He magnified your reward and your rank, since He made your warning general to all of mankind, and singled you out with it so that your reward would increase, for reward comes in proportion to the abundance of striving, and so that He would gather for you the good deeds of those who believe in you, since you are their founder.

﴿So do not obey the disbelievers.﴾ This means the disbelievers of Quraysh. They had listened to him and desired that he return to the religion of their forefathers, and they would make him king over them and gather great wealth for him. So the Exalted forbade him to obey them, until he would show them that he had no desire for any of that, for his desire was only in calling to God and believing in Him.

﴿And strive against them with it.﴾ That is, with the Qur'an, or with Islam, or with the sword, or by abandoning their obedience. The word *jihadan* (struggle) is a verbal noun described by *kabiran* (great), because it is incumbent upon him, peace be upon him, to strive against the entire world, so it is a great struggle.

*Maraja* (he mixed them) means: he mixed the two together, or he poured one of them into the other, or he let them flow; these are opinions. The apparent meaning is that by "the two seas" is meant abundant sweet water and abundant salt water. It has also been said that they are two specific seas: the Sea of Persia and the Sea of Rome. It has been said that they are the sea of the heavens and the sea of the earth, which meet every year; this was reported from Ibn Abbas. Mujahid said: the waters of the rivers that fall into the salt sea, and this is close to the first opinion. Ibn Atiyyah said: the purpose of the verse is to draw attention to the power of God and the perfection of His creation of things, in that He spread in the earth abundant sweet waters from rivers, springs and wells, and placed them amid the bitter water, and placed the bitter water amid them; so you see the sea surrounded on its two banks by sweet waters, and the sea's water reaching the islands and the like, surrounded by bitter water. *Al-barzakh* and *al-hijr* are that which separates the two of them, of earth and barrier; this was said by al-Hasan. This accords with the view of those who say that *maraja* means *ajra* (he let flow). It has also been said that *al-barzakh* refers to the lands and deserts, so the two do not differ except through the removal of the barrier on the Day of Resurrection. Most of the scholars said: the barrier is a prevention from the power of God. Al-Zajjaj said: they are mixed in the sight of the eye, yet separated by the power of God. In Basra, the sweet water flows down from it into the Tigris toward the sea, and the tide comes from the sea, [p. 507] and the two meet without mixing: the sea's water is intensely green, and the Tigris's water is reddish. The water-drawer draws from the Tigris water here with us, and nothing mixes with it. The Nile of Egypt, in its flood, cuts through the salt sea, cutting it in such a way that it remains a flowing reddish river in the middle of the salt water, so that people may draw water from it. The waters appear as pieces in the middle of the salt sea, and people say: this is ice-water, and they give drink from it from the middle of the sea.

Talha and Qutayba, from al-Kisa'i, read *malih* with a fatha on the *mim* and a kasra on the *lam*, and likewise in Fatir. Abu Hatim said: this is an objectionable reading. Abu al-Fath said: he meant *malih* and deleted the alif, as it was deleted from *barad* (cold), meaning *barid*. Abu al-Fadl al-Razi said in the book *al-Lawami*: it is an anomalous and rare dialect. It has been said: he meant *malih* and shortened it by deleting the alif. *Al-malih* is permissible as a description of water, because water is found in the flowing channels being salted by something else, and salty by its own nature. But it is more proper to say *ma'un milh*, described by a verbal noun, meaning: water possessing saltness; and description by this is like *hilf* and *nidw* among attributes.

Al-Zamakhshari said: (If you ask): what is the meaning of ﴿a forbidding ban﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:22)? (I answer): it is the phrase that one who seeks refuge says, and we have explained it. Here it is used figuratively, as if each of the two seas seeks refuge from its companion and says to it: ﴿a forbidding ban﴾, just as He said: ﴿they do not transgress﴾ (Ar-Rahman 55:20), meaning: neither of them transgresses upon its companion by mingling. So the negation of transgression there is like seeking refuge here; He made each of them in the form of one transgressing against its companion, so it seeks refuge from it. This is among the finest metaphors and the clearest evidence of eloquence. End of quotation.

The apparent meaning is that ﴿a forbidding ban﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:22) is conjoined to *barzakh* (a barrier), as an object conjoined to an object; al-Hawfi also parsed it this way. According to what al-Zamakhshari mentioned, it would be by implying an allegorical speech, meaning: and they say—each of the two to its companion—﴿a forbidding ban﴾.

The apparent meaning is the generality of humankind, who are the children of Adam, and *bashar* (human) applies to the singular and the plural. It has been said: by *nasab* (lineage) is meant Adam, and by *sihr* (marriage kinship) is meant Eve. It has been said: *nasab* is the sons and *sihr* the daughters. As for *min al-ma'* (from water), it is either the drop of semen, or that it is the origin of the creation of every living thing. Lineage and marriage kinship cover every relationship between two human beings: lineage is that one shares with another a father and mother, whether near or distant; and marriage kinship is the bonds of marriage. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: lineage is what marriage with it is not permitted, and marriage kinship is the kinship of nursing. From Tawus: nursing is of marriage kinship. From Ali: marriage kinship is what marriage with it is permitted, and lineage is what marriage with it is not permitted. Al-Dahhak said: marriage kinship is the kinship of nursing. Ibn Sirin said: it was revealed concerning the Prophet (ﷺ) and Ali, because lineage and marriage kinship were combined in him. Ibn Atiyyah said: their combining is a sanctity of prohibition until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And your Lord is ever Powerful.﴾ In that He created from one drop of semen a human being of two kinds: male and female.

When He mentioned the signs of His power, and what He bestowed upon His servants of wondrous creations, it was thereby established that He is the one deserving of worship, for He benefits and harms, and this refutes the corrupt intellects of the polytheists who worship idols. The apparent meaning is that *al-kafir* (the disbeliever) is a generic noun, and thus it is general. It has been said: it is Abu Jahl, and the verse was revealed concerning him. Ikrimah said: *al-kafir* here is Iblis. *Al-zahir* and *al-mudahir* are like *al-mu'in* and *al-mu'awin* (helper and assistant); this was said by Mujahid, al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd. The form *fa'il* in the sense of *mufa'il* is common. The meaning is that the disbeliever aids Satan against his Lord through enmity and associating partners with Him. It has been said: the meaning is that the one who does this act, namely worshipping what neither benefits nor harms, is against his Lord, insignificant and despised, from their saying: "I put him behind me (*zahartu bihi*)" when you leave him behind your back and do not turn to him. This is like His saying: ﴿those have no portion﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:77), and the verse continues; this was said by al-Tabari. It has also been said: "against his Lord" means: a helper against the friends of God. It has been said: a helper for the polytheists in preventing God from being declared One.

﴿And We have not sent you except as a bearer of good news and a warner.﴾ He consoled His Prophet with this, meaning: do not be concerned about them, and do not let your soul go to waste over them in sorrows. You are only a Messenger who gives good news to the believers of Paradise and warns the disbelievers of the Fire, and you are not held responsible for their faith, all of them. Then the Exalted commanded him to argue against them, removing the aspects of accusation, with His saying: ﴿Say: I do not ask of you any wage for it﴾, meaning: I do not seek wealth or any benefit that is specifically for me. The pronoun in *'alayhi* (for it) refers to the good news and warning, or to the Qur'an, or to the conveying of the message; there are opinions. The apparent meaning of *illa man sha'a* (except whoever wills) is that it is a disjunctive exception (*istithna' munqati'*, an exception not of the same kind), and this is what the majority said. Accordingly, it has been said: "But whoever wills to take a way to his Lord, let him do so." It has been said: "But whoever spends in the way of God and in striving against His enemies, he is my reward." It has been said that it is a connected exception (*istithna' muttasil*) with an elided noun, its estimate being: except the wage of one who takes a way to his Lord, meaning: except the wage of one who believes, that is, the wage accruing to me for calling him to faith and his acceptance of it, since the Exalted rewards me for that. It has been said: except the wage of one who believes, meaning by the wage the spending in the way of God; that is, I do not ask you for any wage except spending in the way of God, so He made spending the wage.

When He informed that he had weaned himself from asking them for anything, the Exalted commanded him to entrust his affair to Him, to trust Him, and to rely upon Him; He is the one who undertakes His support and the manifestation of His religion. The Exalted described Himself with the attribute which entails trust, in His saying: ﴿the Living who does not die﴾, because this meaning belongs specifically to the Exalted and to no other living being, as He said: ﴿everything perishes except His Face﴾ (Al-Qasas 28:88). One of the early scholars recited this verse and said: it is not valid for a person of intellect to trust, after it, in any created being. Then He commanded him to glorify Him and to praise Him, combined with extolling Him; because glorification has its place in the belief of the heart, and praise has its place in the tongue agreeing with belief. In a hadith: "Whoever says: Glory be to God and praise be to Him, one hundred times, his sins are forgiven even if they were like the foam of the sea." These are the two words that are light upon the tongue and heavy in the scale. ﴿And sufficient is He as one who is aware of the sins of His servants.﴾ He meant that nothing of the affairs of His servants is entrusted to him, whether they believe or disbelieve, and that He is aware of their conditions, sufficient for the recompense of their deeds. In this sentence is consolation for the Messenger and a warning for the disbeliever. In some reports: "Sufficient for you as victory is that your enemy is disobedient." It is an expression intended for emphasis; you say: "Knowledge is sufficient as beauty," and "Good manners are sufficient as wealth," meaning: it is enough for you, you need nothing beyond it, because He is aware of their conditions and able to requite them.

When He commanded him with trust and glorification, and mentioned the attribute of everlasting life, He mentioned what indicates complete power, which is the bringing into being of this world. The discussion of a similar statement has preceded. *Alladhi* (the one who) may be an attribute of *al-Hayy alladhi la yamutu* (the Living who does not die). It becomes definite with the reading of Zayd ibn Ali, *al-Rahmani* in the genitive. As for the reading of the majority, *al-Rahmanu* in the nominative, then *alladhi* may be an attribute of *al-Hayy*, and *al-Rahmanu* the predicate of an elided subject. It may also be that *alladhi* is the subject and *al-Rahmanu* its predicate; or that *alladhi* is the predicate of an elided subject, and *al-Rahmanu* an attribute of it; or that *alladhi* is in the accusative by an implied "I mean." According to the view of al-Akhfash, *al-Rahmanu* may be the subject, and *fas'al* (then ask) its predicate, and it is parsed according to the principle of the poet's saying:

*And a sayer said: "Khawlan, marry their young woman."*

They also permitted that *al-Rahmanu* be a substitute for the concealed pronoun in *istawa* (He established Himself). The apparent meaning is that *bihi* (about Him) is attached to *fas'al* (then ask), and the *ba'* remains un-transposed in the sense of *'an* (about). *Khabiran* (aware) is one of the attributes of God, as you say: "I met Zayd, a lion," and "I met Zayd, the sea," meaning that he is the lion in courage and the sea in generosity. The meaning is that He, the Exalted, is the Subtle, the Knowing, the Aware, and the meaning is: "then ask" God, the Aware of things, the Knower of their realities. Ibn Atiyyah said: *khabiran* on this reading is in the accusative either by the occurrence of the asking, or as a emphasizing circumstantial accusative (*hal mu'akkida*), as He said: ﴿and it is the truth confirming﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:91). This circumstance is not a changing one, since the lofty attribute does not change. End of quotation. This parsing is built on the premise that it is as you say: "If you met so-and-so, you would meet the sea through him in generosity," meaning: you would meet from him. The meaning is: "then ask God about every matter," and its being accusative as an emphasizing circumstantial accusative on this estimate is not valid; it is only valid that it be a direct object. It is permitted that the *ba'* be in the sense of *'an*, meaning: "then ask" about Him, "aware," as the poet said:

*If you ask me about women, then I am knowing of the ailments of women, a physician.*

وهُوَ قَوْلُ الأخْفَشِ والزَّجّاجِ. ويَكُونَ (خَبِيرًا) لَيْسَ مِن صِفاتِ اللَّهِ هُنا، كَأنَّهُ قِيلَ: اسْألْ عَنِ الرَّحْمَنِ الخُبَراءَ جِبْرِيلَ والعُلَماءَ وأهْلَ الكُتُبِ المُنَزَّلَةِ، وإنْ جَعَلْتَ (بِهِ) مُتَعَلِّقًا بِخَبِيرًا كانَ المَعْنى (فاسْألْ) عَنِ اللَّهِ الخُبَراءَ بِهِ. وقالَ الكَلْبِيُّ: مَعْناهُ (فاسْألْ) خَبِيرًا بِهِ، و(بِهِ) يَعُودُ إلى ما ذُكِرَ مِن خَلْقِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ [p-٥٠٩] والِاسْتِواءِ عَلى العَرْشِ، وذَلِكَ الخَبِيرُ هو اللَّهُ تَعالى؛ لِأنَّهُ لا دَلِيلَ في العَقْلِ عَلى كَيْفِيَّةِ خَلْقِ ذَلِكَ، فَلا يَعْلَمُها إلّا اللَّهُ. وعَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ: الخَبِيرُ جِبْرِيلُ وقُدِّمَ لِرُءُوسِ الآيِ. وقالَ الزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ: الباءُ في (بِهِ) صِلَةُ سَلْ، كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿سَألَ سائِلٌ بِعَذابٍ﴾ [المعارج: ١] (أي: "سأل سائل عن عذاب واقع")، كَما يَكُونُ (عَنْ) صِلَتَهُ في نَحْوِ ﴿ثُمَّ لَتُسْألُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ النَّعِيمِ﴾ [التكاثر: ٨] ("ثم لتُسألُنّ يومئذٍ عن النعيم")، أوْ صِلَةُ (خَبِيرًا) بِهِ، فَتَجْعَلُ (خَبِيرًا) مَفْعُولًا، أيْ: فَسَلْ عَنْهُ رَجُلًا عارِفًا يُخْبِرْكَ بِرَحْمَتِهِ، أوْ فَسَلْ رَجُلًا خَبِيرًا بِهِ وبِرَحْمَتِهِ، أوْ فَسَلْ بِسُؤالِهِ خَبِيرًا. كَقَوْلِكَ: رَأيْتُ بِهِ أسَدًا، أيْ: رَأيْتُ بِرُؤْيَتِهِ، والمَعْنى إنْ سَألْتَهُ وجَدْتَهُ خَبِيرًا بِجَعْلِهِ حالًا عَنْ بِهِ تُرِيدُ فَسَلْ عَنْهُ عالِمًا بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ. وقِيلَ: (الرَّحْمَنُ) اسْمٌ مِن أسْماءِ اللَّهِ مَذْكُورٌ في الكُتُبِ المُتَقَدِّمَةِ ولَمْ يَكُونُوا يَعْرِفُونَهُ. فَقِيلَ: فَسَلْ بِهَذا الِاسْمِ مَن يُخْبِرُكَ مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ حَتّى يُعْرَفَ مَن يُنْكِرُهُ، ومِن ثَمَّ كانُوا يَقُولُونَ: ما نَعْرِفُ الرَّحْمَنَ إلّا الَّذِي في اليَمامَةِ يَعْنُونَ مُسَيْلِمَةَ، وكانَ يُقالُ لَهُ رَحْمَنُ اليَمامَةِ، انْتَهى.

﴿وإذا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اسْجُدُوا لِلرَّحْمَنِ﴾ وكانَتْ قُرَيْشٌ لا تَعْرِفُ هَذا في أسْماءِ اللَّهِ غالَطَتْ قُرَيْشٌ بِذَلِكَ فَقالَتْ: إنَّ مُحَمَّدًا يَأْمُرُنا بِعِبادَةِ رَحْمَنِ اليَمامَةِ، نَزَلَتْ ﴿وإذا قِيلَ لَهُمُ﴾، و(ما) سُؤالٌ عَنِ المَجْهُولِ، فَيَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ سُؤالًا عَنِ المُسَمّى بِهِ؛ لِأنَّهم ما كانُوا يَعْرِفُونَهُ بِهَذا الِاسْمِ، ويَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ سُؤالًا عَنْ مَعْناهُ؛ لِأنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ مُسْتَعْمَلًا في كَلامِهِمْ كَما يُسْتَعْمَلُ الرَّحِيمُ والرَّحُومُ والرّاحِمُ، أوْ لِأنَّهم أنْكَرُوا إطْلاقَهُ عَلى اللَّهِ؛ قالَهُ الزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ. والَّذِي يَظْهَرُ أنَّهم لَمّا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ﴿اسْجُدُوا لِلرَّحْمَنِ﴾ فَذُكِرَتِ الصِّفَةُ المُقْتَضِيَةُ لِلْمُبالَغَةِ في الرَّحْمَةِ، والكَلِمَةُ عَرَبِيَّةٌ لا يُنْكَرُ وضْعُها، أظْهَرُوا التَّجاهُلَ بِهَذِهِ الصِّفَةِ الَّتِي لِلَّهِ مُغالَطَةً مِنهم ووَقاحَةً فَقالُوا: ﴿وما الرَّحْمَنُ﴾ ("And what is the Most Merciful?")، وهم عارِفُونَ بِهِ وبِصِفَتِهِ الرَّحْمانِيَّةِ، وهَذا كَما قالَ فِرْعَوْنُ: ﴿وما رَبُّ العالَمِينَ﴾ ("And what is the Lord of the worlds?") [الشعراء: ٢٣] حِينَ قالَ لَهُ مُوسى: ﴿إنّى رَسُولٌ مِن رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ ("I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds") [الأعراف: ١٠٤]، عَلى سَبِيلِ المُناكَرَةِ، وهو عالِمٌ بِرَبِّ العالَمِينَ. كَما قالَ مُوسى: ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ ما أنْزَلَ هَؤُلاءِ إلّا رَبُّ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ بَصائِرَ﴾ ("You certainly know that none has sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidence") [الإسراء: ١٠٢] فَكَذَلِكَ كُفّارُ قُرَيْشٍ اسْتَفْهَمُوا عَنِ الرَّحْمَنِ اسْتِفْهامَ مَن يَجْهَلُهُ، وهم عالِمُونَ بِهِ، فَعَلى قَوْلِ مَن قالَ: لَمْ يَكُونُوا يَعْرِفُونَ الرَّحْمَنَ إلّا مُسَيْلِمَةَ، وعَلى قَوْلِ مَن قالَ: مَن لا يَعْرِفُونَ الرَّحْمَنَ إلّا مُسَيْلِمَةَ. فالمَعْنى أنَسْجَدُ لِمُسَيْلِمَةَ، وعَلى قَوْلِ مَن قالَ: لا يَعْرِفُونَ الرَّحْمَنَ بِالكُلِّيَّةِ فالمَعْنى ﴿أنَسْجُدُ لِما تَأْمُرُنا﴾ ("Shall we prostrate to what you command us?") مِن غَيْرِ عِلْمٍ بِبَيانِهِ. والقائِلُ (اسْجُدُوا) الرَّسُولُ أوِ اللَّهُ عَلى لِسانِ رَسُولِهِ. وقَرَأ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ والأسْوَدُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ وحَمْزَةُ والكِسائِيُّ ”يَأْمُرُ“ بِالياءِ مِن تَحْتُ، أيْ: يَأْمُرُنا مُحَمَّدٌ، والكِنايَةُ عَنْهُ أوِ المُسَمّى الرَّحْمَنَ ولا نَعْرِفُهُ. وقَرَأ باقِي السَّبْعَةِ بِالتّاءِ خِطابًا لِلرَّسُولِ. ومَفْعُولُ (تَأْمُرُنا) الثّانِي مَحْذُوفٌ لِدَلالَةِ الكَلامِ عَلَيْهِ، تَقْدِيرُهُ يَأْمُرُنا سُجُودَهُ نَحْوَ قَوْلِهِمْ: أمَرْتُكَ الخَيْرَ. (وزادَهم) أيْ: هَذا القَوْلُ، وهو الأمْرُ بِالسُّجُودِ لِلرَّحْمَنِ، (زادَهم) ضَلالًا يَخْتَصُّ بِهِ مَعَ ضَلالِهِمُ السّابِقِ، وكانَ حَقُّهُ أنْ يَكُونَ باعِثًا عَلى فِعْلِ السُّجُودِ والقَبُولِ. وقالَ الضَّحّاكُ: سَجَدَ أبُو بَكْرٍ وعُمَرُ وعُثْمانُ وعَلِيٌّ وعُثْمانُ بْنُ مَظْعُونٍ وعَمْرُو ابْنُ غَلَسَةَ، فَرَآهُمُ المُشْرِكُونَ فَأخَذُوا في ناحِيَةِ المَسْجِدِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ، فَهَذا المُرادُ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿وزادَهم نُفُورًا﴾ ("and it increased them in aversion")، ومَعْنى (نُفُورًا): فِرارًا.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 25, verses 51–60 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And had We willed, We would have sent a warner to every town.﴾ When the Exalted knew what the Messenger endured of harm from his people, He informed him that, had He willed, He would have sent a warner to every town, so that the matter would be lighter for you. But He magnified your reward and your rank, since He made your warning general to all of mankind, and singled you out with it so that your reward would increase, for reward comes in proportion to the abundance of striving, and so that He would gather for you the good deeds of those who believe in you, since you are their founder.

﴿So do not obey the disbelievers.﴾ This means the disbelievers of Quraysh. They had listened to him and desired that he return to the religion of their forefathers, and they would make him king over them and gather great wealth for him. So the Exalted forbade him to obey them, until he would show them that he had no desire for any of that, for his desire was only in calling to God and believing in Him.

﴿And strive against them with it.﴾ That is, with the Qur'an, or with Islam, or with the sword, or by abandoning their obedience. The word *jihadan* (struggle) is a verbal noun described by *kabiran* (great), because it is incumbent upon him, peace be upon him, to strive against the entire world, so it is a great struggle.

*Maraja* (he mixed them) means: he mixed the two together, or he poured one of them into the other, or he let them flow; these are opinions. The apparent meaning is that by "the two seas" is meant abundant sweet water and abundant salt water. It has also been said that they are two specific seas: the Sea of Persia and the Sea of Rome. It has been said that they are the sea of the heavens and the sea of the earth, which meet every year; this was reported from Ibn Abbas. Mujahid said: the waters of the rivers that fall into the salt sea, and this is close to the first opinion. Ibn Atiyyah said: the purpose of the verse is to draw attention to the power of God and the perfection of His creation of things, in that He spread in the earth abundant sweet waters from rivers, springs and wells, and placed them amid the bitter water, and placed the bitter water amid them; so you see the sea surrounded on its two banks by sweet waters, and the sea's water reaching the islands and the like, surrounded by bitter water. *Al-barzakh* and *al-hijr* are that which separates the two of them, of earth and barrier; this was said by al-Hasan. This accords with the view of those who say that *maraja* means *ajra* (he let flow). It has also been said that *al-barzakh* refers to the lands and deserts, so the two do not differ except through the removal of the barrier on the Day of Resurrection. Most of the scholars said: the barrier is a prevention from the power of God. Al-Zajjaj said: they are mixed in the sight of the eye, yet separated by the power of God. In Basra, the sweet water flows down from it into the Tigris toward the sea, and the tide comes from the sea, [p. 507] and the two meet without mixing: the sea's water is intensely green, and the Tigris's water is reddish. The water-drawer draws from the Tigris water here with us, and nothing mixes with it. The Nile of Egypt, in its flood, cuts through the salt sea, cutting it in such a way that it remains a flowing reddish river in the middle of the salt water, so that people may draw water from it. The waters appear as pieces in the middle of the salt sea, and people say: this is ice-water, and they give drink from it from the middle of the sea.

Talha and Qutayba, from al-Kisa'i, read *malih* with a fatha on the *mim* and a kasra on the *lam*, and likewise in Fatir. Abu Hatim said: this is an objectionable reading. Abu al-Fath said: he meant *malih* and deleted the alif, as it was deleted from *barad* (cold), meaning *barid*. Abu al-Fadl al-Razi said in the book *al-Lawami*: it is an anomalous and rare dialect. It has been said: he meant *malih* and shortened it by deleting the alif. *Al-malih* is permissible as a description of water, because water is found in the flowing channels being salted by something else, and salty by its own nature. But it is more proper to say *ma'un milh*, described by a verbal noun, meaning: water possessing saltness; and description by this is like *hilf* and *nidw* among attributes.

Al-Zamakhshari said: (If you ask): what is the meaning of ﴿a forbidding ban﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:22)? (I answer): it is the phrase that one who seeks refuge says, and we have explained it. Here it is used figuratively, as if each of the two seas seeks refuge from its companion and says to it: ﴿a forbidding ban﴾, just as He said: ﴿they do not transgress﴾ (Ar-Rahman 55:20), meaning: neither of them transgresses upon its companion by mingling. So the negation of transgression there is like seeking refuge here; He made each of them in the form of one transgressing against its companion, so it seeks refuge from it. This is among the finest metaphors and the clearest evidence of eloquence. End of quotation.

The apparent meaning is that ﴿a forbidding ban﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:22) is conjoined to *barzakh* (a barrier), as an object conjoined to an object; al-Hawfi also parsed it this way. According to what al-Zamakhshari mentioned, it would be by implying an allegorical speech, meaning: and they say—each of the two to its companion—﴿a forbidding ban﴾.

The apparent meaning is the generality of humankind, who are the children of Adam, and *bashar* (human) applies to the singular and the plural. It has been said: by *nasab* (lineage) is meant Adam, and by *sihr* (marriage kinship) is meant Eve. It has been said: *nasab* is the sons and *sihr* the daughters. As for *min al-ma'* (from water), it is either the drop of semen, or that it is the origin of the creation of every living thing. Lineage and marriage kinship cover every relationship between two human beings: lineage is that one shares with another a father and mother, whether near or distant; and marriage kinship is the bonds of marriage. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: lineage is what marriage with it is not permitted, and marriage kinship is the kinship of nursing. From Tawus: nursing is of marriage kinship. From Ali: marriage kinship is what marriage with it is permitted, and lineage is what marriage with it is not permitted. Al-Dahhak said: marriage kinship is the kinship of nursing. Ibn Sirin said: it was revealed concerning the Prophet (ﷺ) and Ali, because lineage and marriage kinship were combined in him. Ibn Atiyyah said: their combining is a sanctity of prohibition until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And your Lord is ever Powerful.﴾ In that He created from one drop of semen a human being of two kinds: male and female.

When He mentioned the signs of His power, and what He bestowed upon His servants of wondrous creations, it was thereby established that He is the one deserving of worship, for He benefits and harms, and this refutes the corrupt intellects of the polytheists who worship idols. The apparent meaning is that *al-kafir* (the disbeliever) is a generic noun, and thus it is general. It has been said: it is Abu Jahl, and the verse was revealed concerning him. Ikrimah said: *al-kafir* here is Iblis. *Al-zahir* and *al-mudahir* are like *al-mu'in* and *al-mu'awin* (helper and assistant); this was said by Mujahid, al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd. The form *fa'il* in the sense of *mufa'il* is common. The meaning is that the disbeliever aids Satan against his Lord through enmity and associating partners with Him. It has been said: the meaning is that the one who does this act, namely worshipping what neither benefits nor harms, is against his Lord, insignificant and despised, from their saying: "I put him behind me (*zahartu bihi*)" when you leave him behind your back and do not turn to him. This is like His saying: ﴿those have no portion﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:77), and the verse continues; this was said by al-Tabari. It has also been said: "against his Lord" means: a helper against the friends of God. It has been said: a helper for the polytheists in preventing God from being declared One.

﴿And We have not sent you except as a bearer of good news and a warner.﴾ He consoled His Prophet with this, meaning: do not be concerned about them, and do not let your soul go to waste over them in sorrows. You are only a Messenger who gives good news to the believers of Paradise and warns the disbelievers of the Fire, and you are not held responsible for their faith, all of them. Then the Exalted commanded him to argue against them, removing the aspects of accusation, with His saying: ﴿Say: I do not ask of you any wage for it﴾, meaning: I do not seek wealth or any benefit that is specifically for me. The pronoun in *'alayhi* (for it) refers to the good news and warning, or to the Qur'an, or to the conveying of the message; there are opinions. The apparent meaning of *illa man sha'a* (except whoever wills) is that it is a disjunctive exception (*istithna' munqati'*, an exception not of the same kind), and this is what the majority said. Accordingly, it has been said: "But whoever wills to take a way to his Lord, let him do so." It has been said: "But whoever spends in the way of God and in striving against His enemies, he is my reward." It has been said that it is a connected exception (*istithna' muttasil*) with an elided noun, its estimate being: except the wage of one who takes a way to his Lord, meaning: except the wage of one who believes, that is, the wage accruing to me for calling him to faith and his acceptance of it, since the Exalted rewards me for that. It has been said: except the wage of one who believes, meaning by the wage the spending in the way of God; that is, I do not ask you for any wage except spending in the way of God, so He made spending the wage.

When He informed that he had weaned himself from asking them for anything, the Exalted commanded him to entrust his affair to Him, to trust Him, and to rely upon Him; He is the one who undertakes His support and the manifestation of His religion. The Exalted described Himself with the attribute which entails trust, in His saying: ﴿the Living who does not die﴾, because this meaning belongs specifically to the Exalted and to no other living being, as He said: ﴿everything perishes except His Face﴾ (Al-Qasas 28:88). One of the early scholars recited this verse and said: it is not valid for a person of intellect to trust, after it, in any created being. Then He commanded him to glorify Him and to praise Him, combined with extolling Him; because glorification has its place in the belief of the heart, and praise has its place in the tongue agreeing with belief. In a hadith: "Whoever says: Glory be to God and praise be to Him, one hundred times, his sins are forgiven even if they were like the foam of the sea." These are the two words that are light upon the tongue and heavy in the scale. ﴿And sufficient is He as one who is aware of the sins of His servants.﴾ He meant that nothing of the affairs of His servants is entrusted to him, whether they believe or disbelieve, and that He is aware of their conditions, sufficient for the recompense of their deeds. In this sentence is consolation for the Messenger and a warning for the disbeliever. In some reports: "Sufficient for you as victory is that your enemy is disobedient." It is an expression intended for emphasis; you say: "Knowledge is sufficient as beauty," and "Good manners are sufficient as wealth," meaning: it is enough for you, you need nothing beyond it, because He is aware of their conditions and able to requite them.

When He commanded him with trust and glorification, and mentioned the attribute of everlasting life, He mentioned what indicates complete power, which is the bringing into being of this world. The discussion of a similar statement has preceded. *Alladhi* (the one who) may be an attribute of *al-Hayy alladhi la yamutu* (the Living who does not die). It becomes definite with the reading of Zayd ibn Ali, *al-Rahmani* in the genitive. As for the reading of the majority, *al-Rahmanu* in the nominative, then *alladhi* may be an attribute of *al-Hayy*, and *al-Rahmanu* the predicate of an elided subject. It may also be that *alladhi* is the subject and *al-Rahmanu* its predicate; or that *alladhi* is the predicate of an elided subject, and *al-Rahmanu* an attribute of it; or that *alladhi* is in the accusative by an implied "I mean." According to the view of al-Akhfash, *al-Rahmanu* may be the subject, and *fas'al* (then ask) its predicate, and it is parsed according to the principle of the poet's saying:

*And a sayer said: "Khawlan, marry their young woman."*

They also permitted that *al-Rahmanu* be a substitute for the concealed pronoun in *istawa* (He established Himself). The apparent meaning is that *bihi* (about Him) is attached to *fas'al* (then ask), and the *ba'* remains un-transposed in the sense of *'an* (about). *Khabiran* (aware) is one of the attributes of God, as you say: "I met Zayd, a lion," and "I met Zayd, the sea," meaning that he is the lion in courage and the sea in generosity. The meaning is that He, the Exalted, is the Subtle, the Knowing, the Aware, and the meaning is: "then ask" God, the Aware of things, the Knower of their realities. Ibn Atiyyah said: *khabiran* on this reading is in the accusative either by the occurrence of the asking, or as a emphasizing circumstantial accusative (*hal mu'akkida*), as He said: ﴿and it is the truth confirming﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:91). This circumstance is not a changing one, since the lofty attribute does not change. End of quotation. This parsing is built on the premise that it is as you say: "If you met so-and-so, you would meet the sea through him in generosity," meaning: you would meet from him. The meaning is: "then ask God about every matter," and its being accusative as an emphasizing circumstantial accusative on this estimate is not valid; it is only valid that it be a direct object. It is permitted that the *ba'* be in the sense of *'an*, meaning: "then ask" about Him, "aware," as the poet said:

*If you ask me about women, then I am knowing of the ailments of women, a physician.*

وهُوَ قَوْلُ الأخْفَشِ والزَّجّاجِ. ويَكُونَ (خَبِيرًا) لَيْسَ مِن صِفاتِ اللَّهِ هُنا، كَأنَّهُ قِيلَ: اسْألْ عَنِ الرَّحْمَنِ الخُبَراءَ جِبْرِيلَ والعُلَماءَ وأهْلَ الكُتُبِ المُنَزَّلَةِ، وإنْ جَعَلْتَ (بِهِ) مُتَعَلِّقًا بِخَبِيرًا كانَ المَعْنى (فاسْألْ) عَنِ اللَّهِ الخُبَراءَ بِهِ. وقالَ الكَلْبِيُّ: مَعْناهُ (فاسْألْ) خَبِيرًا بِهِ، و(بِهِ) يَعُودُ إلى ما ذُكِرَ مِن خَلْقِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ [p-٥٠٩] والِاسْتِواءِ عَلى العَرْشِ، وذَلِكَ الخَبِيرُ هو اللَّهُ تَعالى؛ لِأنَّهُ لا دَلِيلَ في العَقْلِ عَلى كَيْفِيَّةِ خَلْقِ ذَلِكَ، فَلا يَعْلَمُها إلّا اللَّهُ. وعَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ: الخَبِيرُ جِبْرِيلُ وقُدِّمَ لِرُءُوسِ الآيِ. وقالَ الزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ: الباءُ في (بِهِ) صِلَةُ سَلْ، كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿سَألَ سائِلٌ بِعَذابٍ﴾ [المعارج: ١] (أي: "سأل سائل عن عذاب واقع")، كَما يَكُونُ (عَنْ) صِلَتَهُ في نَحْوِ ﴿ثُمَّ لَتُسْألُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ النَّعِيمِ﴾ [التكاثر: ٨] ("ثم لتُسألُنّ يومئذٍ عن النعيم")، أوْ صِلَةُ (خَبِيرًا) بِهِ، فَتَجْعَلُ (خَبِيرًا) مَفْعُولًا، أيْ: فَسَلْ عَنْهُ رَجُلًا عارِفًا يُخْبِرْكَ بِرَحْمَتِهِ، أوْ فَسَلْ رَجُلًا خَبِيرًا بِهِ وبِرَحْمَتِهِ، أوْ فَسَلْ بِسُؤالِهِ خَبِيرًا. كَقَوْلِكَ: رَأيْتُ بِهِ أسَدًا، أيْ: رَأيْتُ بِرُؤْيَتِهِ، والمَعْنى إنْ سَألْتَهُ وجَدْتَهُ خَبِيرًا بِجَعْلِهِ حالًا عَنْ بِهِ تُرِيدُ فَسَلْ عَنْهُ عالِمًا بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ. وقِيلَ: (الرَّحْمَنُ) اسْمٌ مِن أسْماءِ اللَّهِ مَذْكُورٌ في الكُتُبِ المُتَقَدِّمَةِ ولَمْ يَكُونُوا يَعْرِفُونَهُ. فَقِيلَ: فَسَلْ بِهَذا الِاسْمِ مَن يُخْبِرُكَ مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ حَتّى يُعْرَفَ مَن يُنْكِرُهُ، ومِن ثَمَّ كانُوا يَقُولُونَ: ما نَعْرِفُ الرَّحْمَنَ إلّا الَّذِي في اليَمامَةِ يَعْنُونَ مُسَيْلِمَةَ، وكانَ يُقالُ لَهُ رَحْمَنُ اليَمامَةِ، انْتَهى.

﴿وإذا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اسْجُدُوا لِلرَّحْمَنِ﴾ وكانَتْ قُرَيْشٌ لا تَعْرِفُ هَذا في أسْماءِ اللَّهِ غالَطَتْ قُرَيْشٌ بِذَلِكَ فَقالَتْ: إنَّ مُحَمَّدًا يَأْمُرُنا بِعِبادَةِ رَحْمَنِ اليَمامَةِ، نَزَلَتْ ﴿وإذا قِيلَ لَهُمُ﴾، و(ما) سُؤالٌ عَنِ المَجْهُولِ، فَيَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ سُؤالًا عَنِ المُسَمّى بِهِ؛ لِأنَّهم ما كانُوا يَعْرِفُونَهُ بِهَذا الِاسْمِ، ويَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ سُؤالًا عَنْ مَعْناهُ؛ لِأنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ مُسْتَعْمَلًا في كَلامِهِمْ كَما يُسْتَعْمَلُ الرَّحِيمُ والرَّحُومُ والرّاحِمُ، أوْ لِأنَّهم أنْكَرُوا إطْلاقَهُ عَلى اللَّهِ؛ قالَهُ الزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ. والَّذِي يَظْهَرُ أنَّهم لَمّا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ﴿اسْجُدُوا لِلرَّحْمَنِ﴾ فَذُكِرَتِ الصِّفَةُ المُقْتَضِيَةُ لِلْمُبالَغَةِ في الرَّحْمَةِ، والكَلِمَةُ عَرَبِيَّةٌ لا يُنْكَرُ وضْعُها، أظْهَرُوا التَّجاهُلَ بِهَذِهِ الصِّفَةِ الَّتِي لِلَّهِ مُغالَطَةً مِنهم ووَقاحَةً فَقالُوا: ﴿وما الرَّحْمَنُ﴾ ("And what is the Most Merciful?")، وهم عارِفُونَ بِهِ وبِصِفَتِهِ الرَّحْمانِيَّةِ، وهَذا كَما قالَ فِرْعَوْنُ: ﴿وما رَبُّ العالَمِينَ﴾ ("And what is the Lord of the worlds?") [الشعراء: ٢٣] حِينَ قالَ لَهُ مُوسى: ﴿إنّى رَسُولٌ مِن رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ ("I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds") [الأعراف: ١٠٤]، عَلى سَبِيلِ المُناكَرَةِ، وهو عالِمٌ بِرَبِّ العالَمِينَ. كَما قالَ مُوسى: ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ ما أنْزَلَ هَؤُلاءِ إلّا رَبُّ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ بَصائِرَ﴾ ("You certainly know that none has sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidence") [الإسراء: ١٠٢] فَكَذَلِكَ كُفّارُ قُرَيْشٍ اسْتَفْهَمُوا عَنِ الرَّحْمَنِ اسْتِفْهامَ مَن يَجْهَلُهُ، وهم عالِمُونَ بِهِ، فَعَلى قَوْلِ مَن قالَ: لَمْ يَكُونُوا يَعْرِفُونَ الرَّحْمَنَ إلّا مُسَيْلِمَةَ، وعَلى قَوْلِ مَن قالَ: مَن لا يَعْرِفُونَ الرَّحْمَنَ إلّا مُسَيْلِمَةَ. فالمَعْنى أنَسْجَدُ لِمُسَيْلِمَةَ، وعَلى قَوْلِ مَن قالَ: لا يَعْرِفُونَ الرَّحْمَنَ بِالكُلِّيَّةِ فالمَعْنى ﴿أنَسْجُدُ لِما تَأْمُرُنا﴾ ("Shall we prostrate to what you command us?") مِن غَيْرِ عِلْمٍ بِبَيانِهِ. والقائِلُ (اسْجُدُوا) الرَّسُولُ أوِ اللَّهُ عَلى لِسانِ رَسُولِهِ. وقَرَأ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ والأسْوَدُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ وحَمْزَةُ والكِسائِيُّ ”يَأْمُرُ“ بِالياءِ مِن تَحْتُ، أيْ: يَأْمُرُنا مُحَمَّدٌ، والكِنايَةُ عَنْهُ أوِ المُسَمّى الرَّحْمَنَ ولا نَعْرِفُهُ. وقَرَأ باقِي السَّبْعَةِ بِالتّاءِ خِطابًا لِلرَّسُولِ. ومَفْعُولُ (تَأْمُرُنا) الثّانِي مَحْذُوفٌ لِدَلالَةِ الكَلامِ عَلَيْهِ، تَقْدِيرُهُ يَأْمُرُنا سُجُودَهُ نَحْوَ قَوْلِهِمْ: أمَرْتُكَ الخَيْرَ. (وزادَهم) أيْ: هَذا القَوْلُ، وهو الأمْرُ بِالسُّجُودِ لِلرَّحْمَنِ، (زادَهم) ضَلالًا يَخْتَصُّ بِهِ مَعَ ضَلالِهِمُ السّابِقِ، وكانَ حَقُّهُ أنْ يَكُونَ باعِثًا عَلى فِعْلِ السُّجُودِ والقَبُولِ. وقالَ الضَّحّاكُ: سَجَدَ أبُو بَكْرٍ وعُمَرُ وعُثْمانُ وعَلِيٌّ وعُثْمانُ بْنُ مَظْعُونٍ وعَمْرُو ابْنُ غَلَسَةَ، فَرَآهُمُ المُشْرِكُونَ فَأخَذُوا في ناحِيَةِ المَسْجِدِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ، فَهَذا المُرادُ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿وزادَهم نُفُورًا﴾ ("and it increased them in aversion")، ومَعْنى (نُفُورًا): فِرارًا.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 25, verses 51–60 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And had We willed, We would have sent a warner to every town.﴾ When the Exalted knew what the Messenger endured of harm from his people, He informed him that, had He willed, He would have sent a warner to every town, so that the matter would be lighter for you. But He magnified your reward and your rank, since He made your warning general to all of mankind, and singled you out with it so that your reward would increase, for reward comes in proportion to the abundance of striving, and so that He would gather for you the good deeds of those who believe in you, since you are their founder.

﴿So do not obey the disbelievers.﴾ This means the disbelievers of Quraysh. They had listened to him and desired that he return to the religion of their forefathers, and they would make him king over them and gather great wealth for him. So the Exalted forbade him to obey them, until he would show them that he had no desire for any of that, for his desire was only in calling to God and believing in Him.

﴿And strive against them with it.﴾ That is, with the Qur'an, or with Islam, or with the sword, or by abandoning their obedience. The word *jihadan* (struggle) is a verbal noun described by *kabiran* (great), because it is incumbent upon him, peace be upon him, to strive against the entire world, so it is a great struggle.

*Maraja* (he mixed them) means: he mixed the two together, or he poured one of them into the other, or he let them flow; these are opinions. The apparent meaning is that by "the two seas" is meant abundant sweet water and abundant salt water. It has also been said that they are two specific seas: the Sea of Persia and the Sea of Rome. It has been said that they are the sea of the heavens and the sea of the earth, which meet every year; this was reported from Ibn Abbas. Mujahid said: the waters of the rivers that fall into the salt sea, and this is close to the first opinion. Ibn Atiyyah said: the purpose of the verse is to draw attention to the power of God and the perfection of His creation of things, in that He spread in the earth abundant sweet waters from rivers, springs and wells, and placed them amid the bitter water, and placed the bitter water amid them; so you see the sea surrounded on its two banks by sweet waters, and the sea's water reaching the islands and the like, surrounded by bitter water. *Al-barzakh* and *al-hijr* are that which separates the two of them, of earth and barrier; this was said by al-Hasan. This accords with the view of those who say that *maraja* means *ajra* (he let flow). It has also been said that *al-barzakh* refers to the lands and deserts, so the two do not differ except through the removal of the barrier on the Day of Resurrection. Most of the scholars said: the barrier is a prevention from the power of God. Al-Zajjaj said: they are mixed in the sight of the eye, yet separated by the power of God. In Basra, the sweet water flows down from it into the Tigris toward the sea, and the tide comes from the sea, [p. 507] and the two meet without mixing: the sea's water is intensely green, and the Tigris's water is reddish. The water-drawer draws from the Tigris water here with us, and nothing mixes with it. The Nile of Egypt, in its flood, cuts through the salt sea, cutting it in such a way that it remains a flowing reddish river in the middle of the salt water, so that people may draw water from it. The waters appear as pieces in the middle of the salt sea, and people say: this is ice-water, and they give drink from it from the middle of the sea.

Talha and Qutayba, from al-Kisa'i, read *malih* with a fatha on the *mim* and a kasra on the *lam*, and likewise in Fatir. Abu Hatim said: this is an objectionable reading. Abu al-Fath said: he meant *malih* and deleted the alif, as it was deleted from *barad* (cold), meaning *barid*. Abu al-Fadl al-Razi said in the book *al-Lawami*: it is an anomalous and rare dialect. It has been said: he meant *malih* and shortened it by deleting the alif. *Al-malih* is permissible as a description of water, because water is found in the flowing channels being salted by something else, and salty by its own nature. But it is more proper to say *ma'un milh*, described by a verbal noun, meaning: water possessing saltness; and description by this is like *hilf* and *nidw* among attributes.

Al-Zamakhshari said: (If you ask): what is the meaning of ﴿a forbidding ban﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:22)? (I answer): it is the phrase that one who seeks refuge says, and we have explained it. Here it is used figuratively, as if each of the two seas seeks refuge from its companion and says to it: ﴿a forbidding ban﴾, just as He said: ﴿they do not transgress﴾ (Ar-Rahman 55:20), meaning: neither of them transgresses upon its companion by mingling. So the negation of transgression there is like seeking refuge here; He made each of them in the form of one transgressing against its companion, so it seeks refuge from it. This is among the finest metaphors and the clearest evidence of eloquence. End of quotation.

The apparent meaning is that ﴿a forbidding ban﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:22) is conjoined to *barzakh* (a barrier), as an object conjoined to an object; al-Hawfi also parsed it this way. According to what al-Zamakhshari mentioned, it would be by implying an allegorical speech, meaning: and they say—each of the two to its companion—﴿a forbidding ban﴾.

The apparent meaning is the generality of humankind, who are the children of Adam, and *bashar* (human) applies to the singular and the plural. It has been said: by *nasab* (lineage) is meant Adam, and by *sihr* (marriage kinship) is meant Eve. It has been said: *nasab* is the sons and *sihr* the daughters. As for *min al-ma'* (from water), it is either the drop of semen, or that it is the origin of the creation of every living thing. Lineage and marriage kinship cover every relationship between two human beings: lineage is that one shares with another a father and mother, whether near or distant; and marriage kinship is the bonds of marriage. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: lineage is what marriage with it is not permitted, and marriage kinship is the kinship of nursing. From Tawus: nursing is of marriage kinship. From Ali: marriage kinship is what marriage with it is permitted, and lineage is what marriage with it is not permitted. Al-Dahhak said: marriage kinship is the kinship of nursing. Ibn Sirin said: it was revealed concerning the Prophet (ﷺ) and Ali, because lineage and marriage kinship were combined in him. Ibn Atiyyah said: their combining is a sanctity of prohibition until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And your Lord is ever Powerful.﴾ In that He created from one drop of semen a human being of two kinds: male and female.

When He mentioned the signs of His power, and what He bestowed upon His servants of wondrous creations, it was thereby established that He is the one deserving of worship, for He benefits and harms, and this refutes the corrupt intellects of the polytheists who worship idols. The apparent meaning is that *al-kafir* (the disbeliever) is a generic noun, and thus it is general. It has been said: it is Abu Jahl, and the verse was revealed concerning him. Ikrimah said: *al-kafir* here is Iblis. *Al-zahir* and *al-mudahir* are like *al-mu'in* and *al-mu'awin* (helper and assistant); this was said by Mujahid, al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd. The form *fa'il* in the sense of *mufa'il* is common. The meaning is that the disbeliever aids Satan against his Lord through enmity and associating partners with Him. It has been said: the meaning is that the one who does this act, namely worshipping what neither benefits nor harms, is against his Lord, insignificant and despised, from their saying: "I put him behind me (*zahartu bihi*)" when you leave him behind your back and do not turn to him. This is like His saying: ﴿those have no portion﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:77), and the verse continues; this was said by al-Tabari. It has also been said: "against his Lord" means: a helper against the friends of God. It has been said: a helper for the polytheists in preventing God from being declared One.

﴿And We have not sent you except as a bearer of good news and a warner.﴾ He consoled His Prophet with this, meaning: do not be concerned about them, and do not let your soul go to waste over them in sorrows. You are only a Messenger who gives good news to the believers of Paradise and warns the disbelievers of the Fire, and you are not held responsible for their faith, all of them. Then the Exalted commanded him to argue against them, removing the aspects of accusation, with His saying: ﴿Say: I do not ask of you any wage for it﴾, meaning: I do not seek wealth or any benefit that is specifically for me. The pronoun in *'alayhi* (for it) refers to the good news and warning, or to the Qur'an, or to the conveying of the message; there are opinions. The apparent meaning of *illa man sha'a* (except whoever wills) is that it is a disjunctive exception (*istithna' munqati'*, an exception not of the same kind), and this is what the majority said. Accordingly, it has been said: "But whoever wills to take a way to his Lord, let him do so." It has been said: "But whoever spends in the way of God and in striving against His enemies, he is my reward." It has been said that it is a connected exception (*istithna' muttasil*) with an elided noun, its estimate being: except the wage of one who takes a way to his Lord, meaning: except the wage of one who believes, that is, the wage accruing to me for calling him to faith and his acceptance of it, since the Exalted rewards me for that. It has been said: except the wage of one who believes, meaning by the wage the spending in the way of God; that is, I do not ask you for any wage except spending in the way of God, so He made spending the wage.

When He informed that he had weaned himself from asking them for anything, the Exalted commanded him to entrust his affair to Him, to trust Him, and to rely upon Him; He is the one who undertakes His support and the manifestation of His religion. The Exalted described Himself with the attribute which entails trust, in His saying: ﴿the Living who does not die﴾, because this meaning belongs specifically to the Exalted and to no other living being, as He said: ﴿everything perishes except His Face﴾ (Al-Qasas 28:88). One of the early scholars recited this verse and said: it is not valid for a person of intellect to trust, after it, in any created being. Then He commanded him to glorify Him and to praise Him, combined with extolling Him; because glorification has its place in the belief of the heart, and praise has its place in the tongue agreeing with belief. In a hadith: "Whoever says: Glory be to God and praise be to Him, one hundred times, his sins are forgiven even if they were like the foam of the sea." These are the two words that are light upon the tongue and heavy in the scale. ﴿And sufficient is He as one who is aware of the sins of His servants.﴾ He meant that nothing of the affairs of His servants is entrusted to him, whether they believe or disbelieve, and that He is aware of their conditions, sufficient for the recompense of their deeds. In this sentence is consolation for the Messenger and a warning for the disbeliever. In some reports: "Sufficient for you as victory is that your enemy is disobedient." It is an expression intended for emphasis; you say: "Knowledge is sufficient as beauty," and "Good manners are sufficient as wealth," meaning: it is enough for you, you need nothing beyond it, because He is aware of their conditions and able to requite them.

When He commanded him with trust and glorification, and mentioned the attribute of everlasting life, He mentioned what indicates complete power, which is the bringing into being of this world. The discussion of a similar statement has preceded. *Alladhi* (the one who) may be an attribute of *al-Hayy alladhi la yamutu* (the Living who does not die). It becomes definite with the reading of Zayd ibn Ali, *al-Rahmani* in the genitive. As for the reading of the majority, *al-Rahmanu* in the nominative, then *alladhi* may be an attribute of *al-Hayy*, and *al-Rahmanu* the predicate of an elided subject. It may also be that *alladhi* is the subject and *al-Rahmanu* its predicate; or that *alladhi* is the predicate of an elided subject, and *al-Rahmanu* an attribute of it; or that *alladhi* is in the accusative by an implied "I mean." According to the view of al-Akhfash, *al-Rahmanu* may be the subject, and *fas'al* (then ask) its predicate, and it is parsed according to the principle of the poet's saying:

*And a sayer said: "Khawlan, marry their young woman."*

They also permitted that *al-Rahmanu* be a substitute for the concealed pronoun in *istawa* (He established Himself). The apparent meaning is that *bihi* (about Him) is attached to *fas'al* (then ask), and the *ba'* remains un-transposed in the sense of *'an* (about). *Khabiran* (aware) is one of the attributes of God, as you say: "I met Zayd, a lion," and "I met Zayd, the sea," meaning that he is the lion in courage and the sea in generosity. The meaning is that He, the Exalted, is the Subtle, the Knowing, the Aware, and the meaning is: "then ask" God, the Aware of things, the Knower of their realities. Ibn Atiyyah said: *khabiran* on this reading is in the accusative either by the occurrence of the asking, or as a emphasizing circumstantial accusative (*hal mu'akkida*), as He said: ﴿and it is the truth confirming﴾ (Al-Baqarah 2:91). This circumstance is not a changing one, since the lofty attribute does not change. End of quotation. This parsing is built on the premise that it is as you say: "If you met so-and-so, you would meet the sea through him in generosity," meaning: you would meet from him. The meaning is: "then ask God about every matter," and its being accusative as an emphasizing circumstantial accusative on this estimate is not valid; it is only valid that it be a direct object. It is permitted that the *ba'* be in the sense of *'an*, meaning: "then ask" about Him, "aware," as the poet said:

*If you ask me about women, then I am knowing of the ailments of women, a physician.*

وهُوَ قَوْلُ الأخْفَشِ والزَّجّاجِ. ويَكُونَ (خَبِيرًا) لَيْسَ مِن صِفاتِ اللَّهِ هُنا، كَأنَّهُ قِيلَ: اسْألْ عَنِ الرَّحْمَنِ الخُبَراءَ جِبْرِيلَ والعُلَماءَ وأهْلَ الكُتُبِ المُنَزَّلَةِ، وإنْ جَعَلْتَ (بِهِ) مُتَعَلِّقًا بِخَبِيرًا كانَ المَعْنى (فاسْألْ) عَنِ اللَّهِ الخُبَراءَ بِهِ. وقالَ الكَلْبِيُّ: مَعْناهُ (فاسْألْ) خَبِيرًا بِهِ، و(بِهِ) يَعُودُ إلى ما ذُكِرَ مِن خَلْقِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ [p-٥٠٩] والِاسْتِواءِ عَلى العَرْشِ، وذَلِكَ الخَبِيرُ هو اللَّهُ تَعالى؛ لِأنَّهُ لا دَلِيلَ في العَقْلِ عَلى كَيْفِيَّةِ خَلْقِ ذَلِكَ، فَلا يَعْلَمُها إلّا اللَّهُ. وعَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ: الخَبِيرُ جِبْرِيلُ وقُدِّمَ لِرُءُوسِ الآيِ. وقالَ الزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ: الباءُ في (بِهِ) صِلَةُ سَلْ، كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿سَألَ سائِلٌ بِعَذابٍ﴾ [المعارج: ١] (أي: "سأل سائل عن عذاب واقع")، كَما يَكُونُ (عَنْ) صِلَتَهُ في نَحْوِ ﴿ثُمَّ لَتُسْألُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ النَّعِيمِ﴾ [التكاثر: ٨] ("ثم لتُسألُنّ يومئذٍ عن النعيم")، أوْ صِلَةُ (خَبِيرًا) بِهِ، فَتَجْعَلُ (خَبِيرًا) مَفْعُولًا، أيْ: فَسَلْ عَنْهُ رَجُلًا عارِفًا يُخْبِرْكَ بِرَحْمَتِهِ، أوْ فَسَلْ رَجُلًا خَبِيرًا بِهِ وبِرَحْمَتِهِ، أوْ فَسَلْ بِسُؤالِهِ خَبِيرًا. كَقَوْلِكَ: رَأيْتُ بِهِ أسَدًا، أيْ: رَأيْتُ بِرُؤْيَتِهِ، والمَعْنى إنْ سَألْتَهُ وجَدْتَهُ خَبِيرًا بِجَعْلِهِ حالًا عَنْ بِهِ تُرِيدُ فَسَلْ عَنْهُ عالِمًا بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ. وقِيلَ: (الرَّحْمَنُ) اسْمٌ مِن أسْماءِ اللَّهِ مَذْكُورٌ في الكُتُبِ المُتَقَدِّمَةِ ولَمْ يَكُونُوا يَعْرِفُونَهُ. فَقِيلَ: فَسَلْ بِهَذا الِاسْمِ مَن يُخْبِرُكَ مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ حَتّى يُعْرَفَ مَن يُنْكِرُهُ، ومِن ثَمَّ كانُوا يَقُولُونَ: ما نَعْرِفُ الرَّحْمَنَ إلّا الَّذِي في اليَمامَةِ يَعْنُونَ مُسَيْلِمَةَ، وكانَ يُقالُ لَهُ رَحْمَنُ اليَمامَةِ، انْتَهى.

﴿وإذا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اسْجُدُوا لِلرَّحْمَنِ﴾ وكانَتْ قُرَيْشٌ لا تَعْرِفُ هَذا في أسْماءِ اللَّهِ غالَطَتْ قُرَيْشٌ بِذَلِكَ فَقالَتْ: إنَّ مُحَمَّدًا يَأْمُرُنا بِعِبادَةِ رَحْمَنِ اليَمامَةِ، نَزَلَتْ ﴿وإذا قِيلَ لَهُمُ﴾، و(ما) سُؤالٌ عَنِ المَجْهُولِ، فَيَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ سُؤالًا عَنِ المُسَمّى بِهِ؛ لِأنَّهم ما كانُوا يَعْرِفُونَهُ بِهَذا الِاسْمِ، ويَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ سُؤالًا عَنْ مَعْناهُ؛ لِأنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ مُسْتَعْمَلًا في كَلامِهِمْ كَما يُسْتَعْمَلُ الرَّحِيمُ والرَّحُومُ والرّاحِمُ، أوْ لِأنَّهم أنْكَرُوا إطْلاقَهُ عَلى اللَّهِ؛ قالَهُ الزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ. والَّذِي يَظْهَرُ أنَّهم لَمّا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ﴿اسْجُدُوا لِلرَّحْمَنِ﴾ فَذُكِرَتِ الصِّفَةُ المُقْتَضِيَةُ لِلْمُبالَغَةِ في الرَّحْمَةِ، والكَلِمَةُ عَرَبِيَّةٌ لا يُنْكَرُ وضْعُها، أظْهَرُوا التَّجاهُلَ بِهَذِهِ الصِّفَةِ الَّتِي لِلَّهِ مُغالَطَةً مِنهم ووَقاحَةً فَقالُوا: ﴿وما الرَّحْمَنُ﴾ ("And what is the Most Merciful?")، وهم عارِفُونَ بِهِ وبِصِفَتِهِ الرَّحْمانِيَّةِ، وهَذا كَما قالَ فِرْعَوْنُ: ﴿وما رَبُّ العالَمِينَ﴾ ("And what is the Lord of the worlds?") [الشعراء: ٢٣] حِينَ قالَ لَهُ مُوسى: ﴿إنّى رَسُولٌ مِن رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ ("I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds") [الأعراف: ١٠٤]، عَلى سَبِيلِ المُناكَرَةِ، وهو عالِمٌ بِرَبِّ العالَمِينَ. كَما قالَ مُوسى: ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ ما أنْزَلَ هَؤُلاءِ إلّا رَبُّ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ بَصائِرَ﴾ ("You certainly know that none has sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidence") [الإسراء: ١٠٢] فَكَذَلِكَ كُفّارُ قُرَيْشٍ اسْتَفْهَمُوا عَنِ الرَّحْمَنِ اسْتِفْهامَ مَن يَجْهَلُهُ، وهم عالِمُونَ بِهِ، فَعَلى قَوْلِ مَن قالَ: لَمْ يَكُونُوا يَعْرِفُونَ الرَّحْمَنَ إلّا مُسَيْلِمَةَ، وعَلى قَوْلِ مَن قالَ: مَن لا يَعْرِفُونَ الرَّحْمَنَ إلّا مُسَيْلِمَةَ. فالمَعْنى أنَسْجَدُ لِمُسَيْلِمَةَ، وعَلى قَوْلِ مَن قالَ: لا يَعْرِفُونَ الرَّحْمَنَ بِالكُلِّيَّةِ فالمَعْنى ﴿أنَسْجُدُ لِما تَأْمُرُنا﴾ ("Shall we prostrate to what you command us?") مِن غَيْرِ عِلْمٍ بِبَيانِهِ. والقائِلُ (اسْجُدُوا) الرَّسُولُ أوِ اللَّهُ عَلى لِسانِ رَسُولِهِ. وقَرَأ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ والأسْوَدُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ وحَمْزَةُ والكِسائِيُّ ”يَأْمُرُ“ بِالياءِ مِن تَحْتُ، أيْ: يَأْمُرُنا مُحَمَّدٌ، والكِنايَةُ عَنْهُ أوِ المُسَمّى الرَّحْمَنَ ولا نَعْرِفُهُ. وقَرَأ باقِي السَّبْعَةِ بِالتّاءِ خِطابًا لِلرَّسُولِ. ومَفْعُولُ (تَأْمُرُنا) الثّانِي مَحْذُوفٌ لِدَلالَةِ الكَلامِ عَلَيْهِ، تَقْدِيرُهُ يَأْمُرُنا سُجُودَهُ نَحْوَ قَوْلِهِمْ: أمَرْتُكَ الخَيْرَ. (وزادَهم) أيْ: هَذا القَوْلُ، وهو الأمْرُ بِالسُّجُودِ لِلرَّحْمَنِ، (زادَهم) ضَلالًا يَخْتَصُّ بِهِ مَعَ ضَلالِهِمُ السّابِقِ، وكانَ حَقُّهُ أنْ يَكُونَ باعِثًا عَلى فِعْلِ السُّجُودِ والقَبُولِ. وقالَ الضَّحّاكُ: سَجَدَ أبُو بَكْرٍ وعُمَرُ وعُثْمانُ وعَلِيٌّ وعُثْمانُ بْنُ مَظْعُونٍ وعَمْرُو ابْنُ غَلَسَةَ، فَرَآهُمُ المُشْرِكُونَ فَأخَذُوا في ناحِيَةِ المَسْجِدِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ، فَهَذا المُرادُ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿وزادَهم نُفُورًا﴾ ("and it increased them in aversion")، ومَعْنى (نُفُورًا): فِرارًا.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 25, verses 51–60 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And had We willed, We would have sent a warner to every town.﴾ When the Exalted knew what the Messenger endured of harm from his people, He informed him that, had He willed, He would have sent a warner to every town, so that the matter would be lighter for you. But He magnified your reward and your rank, since He made your warning general to all of mankind, and singled you out with it so that your reward would increase, for reward comes in proportion to the abundance of striving, and so that He would gather for you the good deeds of those who believe in you, since you are their founder.

﴿So do not obey the disbelievers.﴾ This means the disbelievers of Quraysh. They had listened to him and desired that he return to the religion of their forefathers, and they would make him king over them and gather great wealth for him. So the Exalted forbade him to obey them, until he would show them that he had no desire for any of that, for his desire was only in calling to God and believing in Him.

﴿And strive against them with it.﴾ That is, with the Qur'an, or with Islam, or with the sword, or by abandoning their obedience. The word *jihadan* (struggle) is a verbal noun described by *kabiran* (great), because it is incumbent upon him, peace be upon him, to strive against the entire world, so it is a great struggle.

*Maraja* (he mixed them) means: he mixed the two together, or he poured one of them into the other, or he let them flow; these are opinions. The apparent meaning is that by "the two seas" is meant abundant sweet water and abundant salt water. It has also been said that they are two specific seas: the Sea of Persia and the Sea of Rome. It has been said that they are the sea of the heavens and the sea of the earth, which meet every year; this was reported from Ibn Abbas. Mujahid said: the waters of the rivers that fall into the salt sea, and this is close to the first opinion. Ibn Atiyyah said: the purpose of the verse is to draw attention to the power of God and the perfection of His creation of things, in that He spread in the earth abundant sweet waters from rivers, springs and wells, and placed them amid the bitter water, and placed the bitter water amid them; so you see the sea surrounded on its two banks by sweet waters, and the sea's water reaching the islands and the like, surrounded by bitter water. *Al-barzakh* and *al-hijr* are that which separates the two of them, of earth and barrier; this was said by al-Hasan. This accords with the view of those who say that *maraja* means *ajra* (he let flow). It has also been said that *al-barzakh* refers to the lands and deserts, so the two do not differ except through the removal of the barrier on the Day of Resurrection. Most of the scholars said: the barrier is a prevention from the power of God. Al-Zajjaj said: they are mixed in the sight of the eye, yet separated by the power of God. In Basra, the sweet water flows down from it into the Tigris toward the sea, and the tide comes from the sea, [p. 507] and the two meet without mixing: the sea's water is intensely green, and the Tigris's water is reddish. The water-drawer draws from the Tigris water here with us, and nothing mixes with it. The Nile of Egypt, in its flood, cuts through the salt sea, cutting it in such a way that it remains a flowing reddish river in the middle of the salt water, so that people may draw water from it. The waters appear as pieces in the middle of the salt sea, and people say: this is ice-water, and they give drink from it from the middle of the sea.

Talha and Qutayba, from al-Kisa'i, read *malih* with a fatha on the *mim* and a kasra on the *lam*, and likewise in Fatir. Abu Hatim said: this is an objectionable reading. Abu al-Fath said: he meant *malih* and deleted the alif, as it was deleted from *barad* (cold), meaning *barid*. Abu al-Fadl al-Razi said in the book *al-Lawami*: it is an anomalous and rare dialect. It has been said: he meant *malih* and shortened it by deleting the alif. *Al-malih* is permissible as a description of water, because water is found in the flowing channels being salted by something else, and salty by its own nature. But it is more proper to say *ma'un milh*, described by a verbal noun, meaning: water possessing saltness; and description by this is like *hilf* and *nidw* among attributes.

Al-Zamakhshari said: (If you ask): what is the meaning of ﴿a forbidding ban﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:22)? (I answer): it is the phrase that one who seeks refuge says, and we have explained it. Here it is used figuratively, as if each of the two seas seeks refuge from its companion and says to it: ﴿a forbidding ban﴾, just as He said: ﴿they do not transgress﴾ (Ar-Rahman 55:20), meaning: neither of them transgresses upon its companion by mingling. So the negation of transgression there is like seeking refuge here; He made each of them in the form of one transgressing against its companion, so it seeks refuge from it. This is among the finest metaphors and the clearest evidence of eloquence. End of quotation.

The apparent meaning is that ﴿a forbidding ban﴾ (Al-Furqan 25:22) is conjoined to *barzakh* (a barrier), as an object conjoined to an object; al-Hawfi also parsed it this way. According to what al-Zamakhshari mentioned, it would be by implying an allegorical speech, meaning: and they say—each of the two to its companion—﴿a forbidding ban﴾.

The apparent meaning is the generality of humankind, who are the children of Adam, and *bashar* (human) applies to the singular and the plural. It has been said: by *nasab* (lineage) is meant Adam, and by *sihr* (marriage kinship) is meant Eve. It has been said: *nasab* is the sons and *sihr* the daughters. As for *min al-ma'* (from water), it is either the drop of semen, or that it is the origin of the creation of every living thing. Lineage and marriage kinship cover every relationship between two human beings: lineage is that one shares with another a father and mother, whether near or distant; and marriage kinship is the bonds of marriage. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: lineage is what marriage with it is not permitted, and marriage kinship is the kinship of nursing. From Tawus: nursing is of marriage kinship. From Ali: marriage kinship is what marriage with it is permitted, and lineage is what marriage with it is not permitted. Al-Dahhak said: marriage kinship is the kinship of nursing. Ibn Sirin said: it was revealed concerning the Prophet (ﷺ) and Ali, because lineage and marriage kinship were combined in him. Ibn Atiyyah said: their combining is a sanctity of prohibition until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And your Lord is ever Powerful.﴾ In that He created from one drop of semen a human being of two kinds: male and female.

When He mentioned the signs of His power, and what He bestowed upon His servants of wondrous creations, it was thereby established that He is the one deserving of worship, for He benefits and harms, and this refutes the corrupt intellects of the polytheists who worship idols. The apparent meaning is that *al-kafir* (the disbeliever) is a generic noun, and thus it is general. It has been said: it is Abu Jahl, and the verse was revealed concerning him. Ikrimah said: *al-kafir* here is Iblis. *Al-zahir* and *al-mudahir* are like *al-mu'in* and *al-mu'awin* (helper and assistant); this was said by Mujahid, al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd. The form *fa'il* in the sense of *mufa'il* is common. The meaning is that the disbeliever aids Satan against his Lord through enmity and associating partners with Him. It has been said: the meaning is that the one who does this act, namely worshipping what neither benefits nor harms, is against his Lord, insignificant and despised, from their saying: "I put him behind me (*zahartu bihi*)" when you leave him behind your back and do not turn to him. This is like His saying: ﴿those have no portion﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:77), and the verse continues; this was said by al-Tabari. It has also been said: "against his Lord" means: a helper against the friends of God. It has been said: a helper for the polytheists in preventing God from being declared One.

﴿And We have not sent you except as a bearer of good news and a warner.﴾ He consoled His Prophet with this, meaning: do not be concerned about them, and do not let your soul go to waste over them in sorrows. You are only a Messenger who gives good news to the believers of Paradise and warns the disbelievers of the Fire, and you are not held responsible for their faith, all of them. Then the Exalted commanded him to argue against them, removing the aspects of accusation, with His saying: ﴿Say: I do not ask of you any wage for it﴾, meaning: I do not seek wealth or any benefit that is specifically for me. The pronoun in *'alayhi* (for it) refers to the good news and warning, or to the Qur'an, or to the conveying of the message; there are opinions. The apparent meaning of *illa man sha'a* (except whoever wills) is that it is a disjunctive exception (*istithna' munqati'*, an exception not of the same kind), and this is what the majority said. Accordingly, it has been said: "But whoever wills to take a way to his Lord, let him do so." It has been said: "But whoever spends in the way of God and in striving against His enemies, he is my reward." It has been said that it is a connected exception (*istithna' muttasil*) with an elided noun, its estimate being: except the wage of one who takes a way to his Lord, meaning: except the wage of one who believes, that is, the wage accruing to me for calling him to faith and his acceptance of it, since the Exalted rewards me for that. It has been said: except the wage of one who believes, meaning by the wage the spending in the way of God; that is, I do not ask you for any wage except spending in the way of God, so He made spending the wage.

When He informed that he had weaned himself from asking them for anything, the Exalted commanded him to entrust his affair to Him, to trust Him, and to rely upon Him; He is the one who undertakes His support and the manifestation of His religion. The Exalted described Himself with the attribute which entails trust, in His saying: ﴿the Living who does not die﴾, because this meaning belongs specifically to the Exalted and to no other living being, as He said: ﴿everything perishes except His Face﴾ (Al-Qasas 28:88). One of the early scholars recited this verse and said: it is not valid for a person of intellect to trust, after it, in any created being. Then He commanded him to glorify Him and to praise Him, combined with extolling Him; because glorification has its place in the belief of the heart, and praise has its place in the tongue agreeing with belief. In a hadith: "Whoever says: Glory be to God and praise be to Him, one hundred times, his sins are forgiven even if they were like the foam of the sea."
